fields.sam888\n\n 2016-05-02 04:08\n\nadministr:
Following your instructions in 0006698:0047433 , I get the same result you did, Thank you.

Confirmed on Gramps master.

Create a new family tree.
Import untitled_3.gpkg.
** Dismiss the Warning dialog on import

Select the "Media" category
Select one of the listed media objects to view the result in the bottombar "Media Preview" gramplet you should see the [x]icon for "Missing image image" is shown.
untar the missing images as indicated
reattach each of the images as mentioned (I had to check the '[x] Convert to a relative path' checkbox
check in the "Media Preview" gramplet that the image can now be viewed
Export to a .gpkg (with a new name)
....................
Create a new empty family tree and import the newly created .gpkg
Select the "Media" category
Select one of the listed media objects to view the result in the bottombar "Media Preview" gramplet you should once again see the [x]icon for "Missing image image" is shown.
In your OS's file explorer open the path where the images have been restored and you can confirm that they exist!
fields.dsblank\n\n 2016-05-02 10:37\n\ndevelope: That was a tricky one! Looks like the filenames start with a space character, and it is getting removed along the way.
fields.dougbain\n\n 2016-05-02 20:08\n\nreporte:
BINGO, Doug! That's exactly what was the trouble.

Removing the leading space from the names of the files in the media directory, and also from the media paths allows them to be exported correctly and to appear in a NarWeb report.

I hadn't noticed the leading spaces all this time and the file names were not intended to have them; but they've got introduced along the way somehow. This smells very like the problem we had several years ago with the Place Completion Tool, where additional space characters were getting smuggled into a string when it was copied (bug 0005780).

However, testing has thrown up a new minor bug with the Narweb report - the Page Generation options allow one to enable both 'include images and media objects' and 'create and use only thumbnail-sized images', but they seem be mutually exclusive and it's thumbnails that dominate.
fields.dougbain\n\n 2016-05-03 09:10\n\nreporte:
Thinking back, I probably created the first filename in the set of images by cut and paste, then for the others just copied the first filename and edited that by changing a digit or two in the name string.

It's exactly like bug 0005780.

It's a nasty little bug, because it wasn't sufficient to change the filenames in the media directory and the path names in Media view. I had to track down the links in Notes where the images were used and edit them to give the correct links as well.

It seems there ought to be a warning about cut-and-paste, but I've no idea where you would want to put it!
